paragraphs.source_en: He could not breathe, he laid his hand on his heart to restrain its throbbing. He paced back and forth with huge strides, he embraced Cosette: “Ah! Cosette! I am an unhappy wretch!” said he. Marius was bewildered. He began to catch a glimpse in Jean Valjean of some indescribably lofty and melancholy figure. An unheard-of virtue, supreme and sweet, humble in its immensity, appeared to him. The convict was transfigured into Christ. Marius was dazzled by this prodigy. He did not know precisely what he beheld, but it was grand. In an instant, a hackney-carriage stood in front of the door. Marius helped Cosette in and darted in himself. “Driver,” said he, “Rue de l’Homme Armé, Number 7.” The carriage drove off. “Ah! what happiness!” ejaculated Cosette. “Rue de l’Homme Armé, I did not dare to speak to you of that. We are going to see M. Jean.” “Thy father! Cosette, thy father more than ever.
